title: Security And Site Access
document_title: SSX Master Security and Site Access Activities

items.text: What is protected? | People, property, materials, equipment, information, occupied operations or critical infrastructure
cells: People, property, materials, equipment, information, occupied operations or critical infrastructure

items.text: Where? | Perimeter, gate, building, floor, room, roof, laydown, office, utility area or digital system
cells: Perimeter, gate, building, floor, room, roof, laydown, office, utility area or digital system

items.text: From what risk? | Unauthorized entry, theft, vandalism, violence, trespass, sabotage, information loss or operational disruption
cells: Unauthorized entry, theft, vandalism, violence, trespass, sabotage, information loss or operational disruption

items.text: Who may enter? | Worker, visitor, owner, inspector, delivery driver, emergency responder or authorized specialist
cells: Worker, visitor, owner, inspector, delivery driver, emergency responder or authorized specialist

items.text: When? | Work hours, after hours, weekends, shutdowns, high-risk operations, turnover or occupancy
cells: Work hours, after hours, weekends, shutdowns, high-risk operations, turnover or occupancy

items.text: How is access controlled? | Guard, badge, roster, key, lock, escort, camera, alarm, turnstile or digital credential
cells: Guard, badge, roster, key, lock, escort, camera, alarm, turnstile or digital credential

items.text: Who responds? | Security, superintendent, owner, police, fire department, emergency team or system administrator
cells: Security, superintendent, owner, police, fire department, emergency team or system administrator

items.text: What proves control? | Approved plan, access log, credential record, patrol log, video, incident report or turnover receipt
cells: Approved plan, access log, credential record, patrol log, video, incident report or turnover receipt

items.text: Building, floor, room and access point
Install perimeter, gates, lighting and monitoring
Recover credentials and remove temporary systems
Verify work authorization through employer process
Provide approved appeal or correction path
Never place sensitive screening details in general site logs
Aim to limit glare and nuisance
Control tools and devices when required
Inspect outgoing property under approved policy
Do not place secrets in general project records
Maintain patient, guest, tenant or staff routes
Restore secured condition after each shift
Maintain Knox Box or required access
Protect life and summon emergency assistance
Preserve relevant video and access logs
Phase change → revised access and security
Testing and training → owner security transfer
Badge/key recovery and temporary-system removal → security closeout
Establish security before unrestricted mobilization and material delivery.
Keep emergency access available regardless of security level.
Link credentials to screening, orientation and current work assignment.
Assign access by zone and time rather than granting unnecessary universal access.
Audit active badges, keys and accounts regularly.
Relocate cameras, lighting and guards as workfronts change.
Protect privacy and confidential screening results.
Preserve incident evidence under controlled access.
Integrate door hardware, access control, life safety and owner operations.
Recover credentials and deactivate digital access promptly.
Schedule permanent-system testing, training and transfer before occupancy.
Remove temporary security and restore affected property at closeout.
